seam_notes: pof-mcp already had opt-in group gating keyed on POF_MCP_TOOL_GROUPS but nothing session-scoped: every session got all 50 tools regardless of who connected. Topology now resolves from the MCP initialize handshake's clientInfo (explicit clientInfo.topology first, then a name table), with the env path (POF_MCP_TOPOLOGY, then the HARNESS_MODE/CI shape e2e/helpers/ci-harness.ts uses) kept only as a fallback when the session declares nothing, and 'unknown' when neither speaks — unknown advertises the FULL surface, so an absent marker is never rendered as 'no editor'. Measured with the env vars blank: editor 50 tools, headless 46, web 46, nothing-declared 50 (was 50 for all four). The four withheld are the pof-bridge tools that need a live editor; pof_ue_status stays because it is the reachability probe and reports connected:false honestly. The editor-only list is guarded by a test asserting each named tool's own description says it needs a live editor — that guard failed on first run and exposed a real gap: pof_ue_test_results reads through pof-bridge but never said so; its description was corrected rather than the guard weakened. | gate: green — typecheck clean; 75/75 unit tests pass including the two new stdio tests that spawn the real server with HARNESS_MODE/CI/POF_MCP_TOPOLOGY explicitly blank; the 36 contract/quality itests skipped cleanly (PoF backend not running at 127.0.0.1:3001), so the contract lane is unproven rather than failing
falsifier: Set clientInfo.topology to 'editor' with POF_MCP_TOPOLOGY, HARNESS_MODE and CI all unset: if pof_ue_compile is absent from tools/list, the env read is back. Conversely a declared headless session that still lists it means the topology filter was dropped from advertisedTools. The direction is void if every client that reaches pof-mcp is spawned by PoF itself and always carries the marker — untrue today, since the Claude Code CLI connects over stdio from an .mcp.json entry that sets neither.

subject: agent-runtime-assembly
seam: src/lib/harness/run-harness.ts:88,163,188 (themeDirective is a start-time option, read once into HarnessOptions and passed into the orchestrator); tools/pof-mcp/src/tools/harness.ts:143-165 (pof_harness_control exposes exactly two verbs, pause and resume — no verb carries a message); src/lib/harness/run-harness.ts:431,447,452 (harness:paused, harness.pause() — pause is honoured after the current iteration)
seam_notes: The loop has no input door. The only mid-run levers are pause and resume, and direction is fixed at construction. An UNDESIGNED injection path exists and works: pause is honoured after the current iteration, and resume with a statePath rehydrates from run-meta.json + harness-config.json on disk rather than from the lost in-memory orchestrator (a deliberate crash-safety choice), so an operator can pause, hand-edit the config the resume reads, and resume with a changed direction while the run keeps its identity and history. It has no record of the intervention, no ordering guarantee against the pause it races, and leaves nothing in the run's history showing that a person intervened or when. Deliberately not proposed here: building the injection door. That is a direction-sized change to the harness's control surface, not a coverage fix, and it is the owner's call.
measure: None taken, and that is the finding. The claim 'a first-class boundary injection beats hand-editing a config file under a race' is a design argument about operator outcomes, and nothing in this tree counts operator outcomes.
falsifier: The instrument that would settle it half exists: the harness emits lifecycle events including harness:paused, and every run writes durable run-meta.json. Counting, per run, whether a pause was followed by a resume of the SAME run or by a fresh start — and how many areas were replanned when it was a fresh start — yields the number this technique moves: work discarded per operator intervention. Until that counter exists the verdict cannot be better or not-better. RETURN CONDITION: when the harness gains that counter, or when an operator reports discarding a plan to change direction.
